terms.comment: Our description: a tall chair, in which a small child sits up at the table. No ancient name is known, and Traupman, Morgan–Owens and Levi–Bini give none.

phrases.latin: Tē in sellam altam impōnam; tum cēnābimus.
phrases.english: I’ll lift you into your high chair; then we’ll have supper.

sources: Lewis & Short: sella · Lewis & Short: altus · Lewis & Short: impono
Traupman, Morgan–Owens and Levi–Bini have no word for a high chair (searched under high chair, highchair, and Italian seggiolone).
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
